sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The verb form usually shows who is doing the action, so Hungarian often leaves the subject pronoun unstated.

This is exactly why listening comprehension is harder before your ear knows the endings — miss the last syllable of a Hungarian verb and you can lose track of who’s being talked about entirely, since there’s often no pronoun to fall back on. Training your ear on verb endings pays off doubly for this reason.
